title: intake.v1
description: The DRAFT contract for the intake surface (§2, task A4): request bodies for PUT /v2/entries and POST /v2/entries/remove, the shared success Reply envelope (§2.4, ten results), the Meeting object every reply/read/webhook renders (meeting_api.intake.projection.project_meeting), the EntryState row GET /v2/entries returns, and the Error envelope (§2.5). UNSEALED — not yet in contracts.seal.json; sealed in task A8 once the routes are built against it. `start`/`end`/timestamp-shaped fields intentionally use a loose ISO-8601 `pattern`, not `format: date-time`, so a NAIVE timestamp (no offset) still conforms at the schema layer — rejecting it is validation.py's own step 2 (§2, validation order), kept distinct from the schema step so the two produce the SAME invalid_request code from two different, testable causes.

Entry.description: PUT /v2/entries request body (§2.2). start/end are required unless join_now is true (§2.2: 'Instant join is decided by this flag only, never by the external_id').

external_id.description: The sender's own id, any format; aw-bots never parses it. Unique per (account, user).

meeting_url.description: One link, chosen by the sender. Parsed by aw-bots elsewhere; unknown -> unrecognized_link (not a schema-level check).

start.description: ISO 8601; offset required by validation.py step 2, not by this pattern.

end.description: Must be after start (validation.py step 5, not a schema-level check).

metadata.description: <= 16384 bytes of canonical JSON; the byte-size check is validation.py step 4, not a schema-level check (JSON Schema has no serialized-byte-length keyword).

reason.description: cancelled | declined | deleted | moved_out_of_window | not_eligible, or free text. Recorded and sent in the webhook.

ReplyEntry.description: The small `entry` block inside Reply (§2.4) — NOT the full EntryState row.

state.description: 'active' | 'removed' — this entry's own state after the operation.

Outcome.description: Meeting.outcome (§2.4) — null until the meeting ends with no bot, or a scheduled entry is superseded. kind/detail are intake-owned; not the lifecycle.v1 BotStatus/CompletionReason vocabulary.

Export.description: Meeting.export (§2.4) — null until the exporter reports a result.

MeetingEntryRef.description: One item of Meeting.entries (§2.4) — active entries only (meeting_api.intake.projection._entry).

Meeting.description: The §2.4 meeting object — exactly the 16 keys meeting_api.intake.projection.project_meeting renders, in this order. Every reply, read and webhook ships a meeting through this one shape.

id.description: str(meetings.uuid) — never the integer row id.

Reply.description: Every successful call (§2.4): HTTP 200. `result` is one of the ten outcomes; `meeting` is always the full projection (project_meeting never returns null).

previous_meeting_id.description: Set only for 'updated' when the entry moved off a meeting.

EntryState.description: GET /v2/entries row (§2.1): the entry's own §2.2 fields, plus content_hash and state, so a sender can diff its view against aw-bots'.

Error.description: Every error (§2.5). The gateway uses the same shape for /v2 auth and rate errors. `message` never echoes `metadata` or the URL query string (validation.py never builds one from either).
